Subject: Re: Performance questionnaire: latency/throughput and burst tolerance

Hi Tom — attached are the artifacts we discussed: a one-page summary plus the full burst/soak report. Below are the highlights and short methodology notes. Full CSVs are in the attached workbook.

Summary (representative numbers, single model variant = LlamaX-13B):
- Generative (2k tokens):
  - 5 qps: p50 78 ms, p95 210 ms, p99 480 ms (A100, fp16, batching=auto, avg tokens/sec per GPU 2400)
  - 50 qps: p50 89 ms, p95 360 ms, p99 920 ms (A100, fp16, batching=dynamic, sustained throughput uses multi-GPU routing)
  - 200 qps: p50 120 ms, p95 650 ms, p99 2.1 s (H100, int8 quant, aggressive batching, sustained throughput measured with 16-GPU pool)
- Embeddings (128 tokens):
  - 5/50/200 qps: p50 ~12 ms, p95 ~28 ms, p99 ~72 ms (measured on A100, fp16; embeddings are cheaper per-token so tail is tighter)

Test harness and methodology (short):
- Traffic generator: Locust + custom client that replays realistic inter-arrival distributions (Poisson + heavy tail bursts).
- Warmup: each run includes 5 minutes of gradual ramp to prime KV caches and JIT paths. Cold-start tests start from stopped GPUs and include model load time measurements.
- Batching: we used Redwood continuous-batching layer with target max_batch_size=128 and an adaptive latency SLO control that backs off batch size to keep p95 under target when specified.
- Metrics collection: Server-side tracing (per-token timing), host-level telemetry (GPU utilization, PCIe), and client-side latency samples; we report p50/p95/p99 over 5 repeated runs.

Burst behaviour (5x-10x for 1–2 minutes):
- Typical behavior: immediate increase in p95/p99 (2–4x) as queues grow; p50 moves less. Error rates remain low if headroom exists, otherwise the runtime will shed work via fast-fail queue rejection or fallback to a smaller model variant.
- Recommended strategies:
  - Reserve a modest burst buffer (10–15% extra capacity) at Dedicated level for customer workloads that need deterministic bursts.
  - Enable model-variant fallback (e.g., 13B -> 7B quantized) with transparent routing to preserve success rate while degrading quality.
  - Client-side retries with jitter and circuit-breaker for persistent over-saturation.

Attachments: redwood_throughput_burst_report.pdf (summary + curves), test-harness-config-2027.yaml, novatech_perf_matrix_v1.xlsx (raw samples).

Happy to run the live 10x burst on Wed if that still works.

—Grace O'Connor
Performance Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@novatech.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Performance questionnaire: latency/throughput and burst tolerance

Tom — quick technical reply to the two bullets you called out. Short answer: the short 8–12s spikes are predominantly queueing effects when headroom is low; cold-model loads are a separate signal we can measure and mitigate. Details and recommended settings below.

What causes the p99 spike:
- Queueing under saturated workers — when incoming rate exceeds processing capacity the runtime accumulates requests in per-worker queues which increases p95/p99 quickly.
- Cold load contributes when there's model churn (scale out/in) during the spike, but for short 12s bursts this is usually secondary unless you have aggressive autoscale delays.

Recommended configuration for NovaTech profile:
- Warm pools: maintain a small warm pool complement sized to absorb expected burst magnitude (we recommend warm_pool = ceil(0.2 * baseline_active_gpus)).
- Fast-fail thresholds: set server-side queue length thresholds and prefer graceful degradation over queueing (reject at 95th percentile queue depth), returning a small structured fallback token so the client can optionally retry.
- Fallback routing: enable a two-tier variant map — primary (13B fp16) and fallback (7B int8) — with sticky routing per session id. Sticky routing preserves ordering by hashing session_id -> routing slot. When a request is routed to a fallback variant, the session_id continues to map to the fallback for the duration of the spike to avoid interleaving variants mid-session.
- Autoscale tuning: use short-scale reaction for bursts (30s policy) but cap scale-out to avoid overprovisioning for short spikes; prefer burst buffers instead.

Expected p99 delta (empirical example from our runs):
- For an 8–10x, 12s burst on a baseline 50 qps gen workload: p99 increases from ~0.9s to ~2.8s if no warm pool or fallback is enabled.
- With warm_pool (15% headroom) + fallback enabled: p99 observed ~1.1–1.5s with <0.5% error rate (measured on H100 cluster, see attached throughput CSV).

Next steps: we can run a targeted 12s 10x replay against your staging keys. We'll need ephemeral access (IP allowlist) to your test harness or a walled-garden endpoint. If you approve, we can schedule the live run and share the raw tracing afterwards.
